generation.final_prompt:
Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: WHY COMPUTE MIGHT GET 10X+ MORE EXPENSIVE IN COMING YEARS
Summary: AI generates more economic value while compute supply grows slowly, so the price of computing power could rise dramatically. This would favor frontier labs with the most efficient models, eliminate lower-value applications, and deepen the concentration of power in the AI industry.

Editorial idea:
The rising economic value of AI collides with a slowly expanding supply of compute, pushing access toward those able to absorb sharply higher costs.

Central subject:
The widening gap between AI ambition and affordable computing capacity.

Visual relationship:
A growing demand presses against a constrained supply, making increasingly valuable AI work harder and more expensive to sustain.

Composition:
Show a narrow passage being progressively occupied by heavier, denser loads on one side while the available route remains fixed and limited; the imbalance should convey rising pressure without depicting literal technology infrastructure.

Permitted literal elements:
A constrained passage
Increasingly heavy abstract loads
A small number of loads advancing while others are held back

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
Racks
Chips
Laptops
Robots
Clouds
Shields
Arrows
Charts
Skyscrapers
Chess
Handshakes
Split-screen conflict
Rendered text
Logos

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting generic AI hardware without showing the supply-and-demand tension
Making the cost increase look like a simple upward chart
Suggesting that all AI applications advance equally despite the summary's emphasis on selection and
Using decorative technology imagery unrelated to compute scarcity

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
